headline: Approved $500,000 study for Horace Mann School repairs and police cameras for Haunted Happenings; referred short-term rental excise to committee.
summary: Council accepted grants for decarbonizing Horace Mann School and voted 9-1-1 to change parking rules for two-family homes. It removed a 2-megawatt limit from a data center zoning ordinance. A proposed excise on short-term rentals for a Housing Stability Fund was referred to committee.
decisions: Canceled the hearing on National Grid's request to install a jointly owned pole at Summit Ave and Eden Street.
Approved the Mayor's appointments of Joe Ferrari, Kathleen Walker and Jill El-Ashkar to the Taxpayer Relief Committee, 10-0-1.
Confirmed the Mayor's reappointments to the Food Policy Council and Public Art Commission, 10-0-1.
Received and filed the Mayor's appointments of Marc Miller and Anthony Barente to the Salem Cultural Council.
Received and filed the Mayor's appointment of Ans Ishfaq as constable.
Approved $105,534.14 for vacation and sick leave buybacks for Ilene Simons and Paul DeFranco.
Referred the home rule petition for a short-term rental excise to the Committee on Administration, co-posted with the Committee of the Whole.
Approved raising the Horace Mann Laboratory School repair study appropriation to $500,000, an increase of $250,000.
Approved accepting $5,000,000, $4,798,587 and $2,483,235 in grants for Horace Mann School decarbonization and electrification.
Denied a motion to suspend the rules and reconsider the City Seal Task Force report vote.
Approved holding the November 12, 2026 and December 3, 2026 regular council meetings.
Approved on second passage the removal of language on aggregate power demand of 2 megawatts or higher from the data center zoning ordinance.
Approved John Tejada's exemption to work part-time as a tutor for Salem Public Schools, up to 500 hours a year.
Approved Salem Police request for temporary video cameras at high-traffic areas during Haunted Happenings; Councillor Holappa opposed.
Denied a motion to refer the police camera request to the Committee on Ordinances, Licenses, and Legal Affairs; it did not receive a second.
Ordered a hearing for October 22, 2026 on National Grid's request to install a pole at Bridge Street and Flint Street.
Granted the Chestnut residents' petition for a block party from Summer Street to Flint Street on October 31, 2026.
Granted the Boys and Girls Club of Greater Salem's request to hold the Wild Turkey 5 Mile Run on November 26, 2026.
Granted a public guide license to Aaron "Mason" Amnott.
Referred claims from Yoselin Cruel-Cabrera and Matthew Gifford to the Committee on Ordinances, Licensees and Legal Affairs.
Approved the bond for Ans Ishfah, which had been referred to committee.
Approved a trial one-way eastbound traffic pattern on Dodge Street from Dodge Street Court to Lafayette Street, October 1 to October 31, 2026.
Approved on second passage the zoning change to required parking for two-family dwellings, 9-1-1.

#492 TO IMPOSE AN EXCISE ON SHORT -TERM RENTALS DEDICATED TO A HOUSING 
STABILITY FUND  
 
Councillor Hapworth recused himself from this matter.  On the motion of Councillor 
Smith seconded by Councillor King the following order was referred to the Committee 
on Administration Co-posted with the Committee of the Whole 
 
ORDERED: That a petition to the General Court, accompanied by a bill for an act 
authorizing the City of Salem to impose an excise on short-term rentals dedicated to a 
Housing Stability Fund as set forth below, be filed with an attested copy of this Order be,
950 
CITY OF SALEM 
OCTOBER 8, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
and hereby is, approved under Clause (1) of Section 8 of Article 2, as amended, of the 
Amendments to the Constitution of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, to the end that 
the following legislation be adopted, except for amendments by the Senate or House of 
Representatives which conform to the intent of this home rule petition: 
  
 AN ACT AUTHORIZING THE CITY OF SALEM TO IMPOSE AN EXCISE ON SHORT -TERM 
RENTALS DEDICATED TO A HOUSING STABILITY FUND 
 
Be it enacted by the Senate and House of Representatives in General Court assembled, 
and by the authority of the same as follows: 
SECTION 1 . Notwithstanding section 14 of chapter 64G of the General Laws or any other 
general or special law to the contrary, the City of Salem is hereby authorized to impose an 
annual excise on the privilege of operating a short-term rental, as defined in the City’s 
short-term rental ordinance, in the City of Salem. The excise shall be payable by the 
operator of the short-term rental in the amount of $1,000 per unit per year for a short-term 
rental of a residential unit that is not the operator’s primary residence, as those terms are 
defined in said ordinance, and $500 per unit per year for all other short-term rentals. The 
City Council may, by ordinance, adjust said amounts annually by not more than the 
percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for the preceding year. The excise shall 
not apply to a short-term rental of a room or rooms within a residential unit that is the 
primary residence of its owner while the owner is present, or to a short-term rental located 
in a lodging house or bed and breakfast licensed or permitted as such by the City. The 
excise shall be in addition to any short-term rental registration fee, room occupancy 
excise, or community impact fee imposed under any other general or special law. 
SECTION 2. The excise authorized by this act shall be adopted by ordinance of the City 
Council of the City of Salem, with the approval of the Mayor, which ordinance shall 
establish the effective date of the excise and provisions for its collection, enforcement, 
and abatement. 
 
 SECTION 3. Not with standing section 53 of chapter 44 of the General Laws or any other 
general or special law to the contrary, the City of Salem is hereby authorized to establish a 
Housing Stability Fund, into which all revenue collected from the excise authorized by this 
act shall be deposited. The Fund may also receive appropriations, gifts, grants, and 
investment earnings. Any balance in the Fund at the close of a fiscal year shall not revert to 
the general fund. Monies in the Fund may be expended, subject to appropriation, only for 
emergency shelter, transitional housing, and homelessness-prevention services, and 
reasonable costs of administering such programs. 
SECTION 4. This act shall take effect upon its passage.

exempt, as would be residents, that periodically rent out their room as the primary 
residence.  This would support the resumption of a local low threshold shelter 
site.  Although no specific location has been determined yet.  If this is approved the city 
would then develop an RFP to identify a site. 
 
Councillor King:  I just want to clarify one of the points that Councillor Davis brought up, 
which is regarding people who are inside their primary residence that rent portions of 
their primary or the entirety  of their primary residence.  The language that was on the 
agenda that was posted publicly said that there was an excise that would not apply to 
units that are the primary residence of the owner. Basically when they rent out rooms or 
part of the rooms of the residential unit where the primary residence of it's owner  lives 
their while the owner is present.  The original thing that we had in front of us basically 
said that it was only exempt when the owner was present in unit.  Which would mean if 
the owner lives in the house and they are just renting out a room while the owner is 
living there that would be the exemption.  The Mayor sent us a version with updated 
language today that removes the language while the owner is present.  Which is 
important for a lot of people here in Salem who only rent out their property for part of the 
year.  Let's say that you live in your house most of the year and you just leave for the 
month of October.  You go and sleep on someone's couch and rent out your house

language that is not on the agenda but is the corrected language that we are voting

An Ordinance Amending a Zoning Ordinance Relative to Data Centers 
Be it ordained by the City Council of the City of Salem, as follows: 
 
Section I. Section 3.1 Table of Principal and Accessory Use Regulations of the City of 
Salem Zoning Ordinance is hereby amended by adding in Section D Industrial Uses, 
after “Contractor’s yard; landscaping business”, the following, shown in underlined and 
italics: 
 
Section II. Section 10.0 Definitions is hereby amended by inserting the following 
definition after the definition for “COOP”: 
Data Center: A facility, or portion thereof, primarily designed or used to house computer 
servers and related information technology infrastructure for the storage, processing, 
management, or transmission of electronic data. A Data Center may include, but is not 
limited to, server racks, data storage systems, cooling systems, power conditioning 
equipment, substations, uninterruptible power supplies, backup generators, 
telecommunications equipment, security systems, and associated mechanical and
956 
CITY OF SALEM 
OCTOBER 8, 2026 
REGULAR MEETING 
 
electrical infrastructure. For purposes of this ordinance, a Data Center shall not be 
considered an Office, Warehouse, Manufacturing, or Research use. A Data Center shall 
not include such computer servers and related information technology infrastructure that 
is accessory, incidental and subordinate to a lawful principal use at the same facility, or 
portion thereof. However, this exception does not cover a separate business providing 
data storage, server hosting, distributed processing, or similar technology to third 
parties. Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, Data Centers are prohibited in 
each and every underlying district, overlay district and special district of this Ordinance. 
 
Section III. This Ordinance shall take effect as provided by City Charter.
